text: A 3-dimensional solid S has a flat base. This base is a region R in the plane. Cross sections of S perpendicular to the y-axis are squares, thus the bases of the squares are the line segments where horizontal lines in the plane intersect R. The region R is in the first quadrant of the plane, bounded below by the z-axis, bounded above by the curve y = e*, and bounded on the right by the line = 3; it is shown shaded in the figure below.
